ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is divided into line graphs for two regions, A and B. Horizontally, both are divided according to Period I, Period II, and Period III, and below it is marked that I is new products, II is mature products, and III is standardized products; the legend shows that the solid line represents production, and the dashed line represents consumption. In Place A, the production curve is relatively high in Periods I and II and grows earlier, indicating that production in the early stage is mainly in Place A; in Place B, the production level is very low in Periods I and II, and by Period III the production curve rises obviously and rapidly, indicating that the production focus later shifts to Place B. Then reason: This process of “new products are first produced in technologically advanced regions, and after the products mature and become standardized, they diffuse and production transfers to other regions” conforms to the product life cycle theory. The most typical enterprise type is enterprises related to electronic products.
